correctness.rationale: For every n>=4 and 2<=a<=n-2, no singleton or nonconsecutive two-set can initially force. Starting at an adjacent pair on the length-a arc, two forcing fronts reach the chord endpoints after i and a-1-i synchronous rounds; an early endpoint is blocked from the opposite arc by its two white neighbors until both endpoints are blue. After T=max(i,a-1-i), the length-b arc fills from both ends in floor(b/2) rounds; swapping arcs gives the other formula. Counting max(i,l-1-i) explicitly gives B_l(z), hence the entire enumerator, bounds, complete realized interval, efficient-set parity and cycle comparison. Boundary a=b=2 and seeds at chord endpoints are covered by the proof. Python directly simulated every chord and every original-cycle starting pair for n=4..50, also every other two-set for n<=12. Independent C++ bit-mask code simulated all two-sets for n=4..22. Both passed from the actual standalone public source paths. Finite tests are corroboration only.

originality.rationale: The nearest source Boyer et al. (arXiv:1801.08910, Theorem 22 Claim 1) already proves exact equality of the forcing-set families of C_n and C_n+e, which is credited. Chilakamarri et al. (arXiv:1105.1492, Observation 2.6(iii)) give the iteration index only for an unchorded cycle; Hogben et al. (arXiv:1410.4191) introduce propagation-time and efficient-set concepts; Ferrero et al. (arXiv:2511.16335) examine time intervals generally. The proposed invariant is the complete round-count distribution for each minimum pair and its multiplicities. Set membership and count do not imply round counts: a chord can change times while preserving every forcing set. Relevant primary sections, search aliases and database records were checked, with the residual risk of an unindexed equivalent result explicitly acknowledged.
residual_risks: No literature search proves historical uniqueness; unindexed notes, theses, or alternate terminology may contain an equivalent timing formula.
Broader propagation-time treatments not named in the selected primary sources may contain an implicit specialization; independently checking all such sources remains future scholarly work.
Previous literature establishes the identical minimum forcing sets, so the claim is confined to dynamic timing and its exact enumeration rather than set identification.

value.rationale: This is a motivated all-parameter refinement of a published equality that says the static zero-forcing polynomial cannot distinguish cycles from singly chorded cycles. The exact dynamic time enumerator does distinguish them; it provides all possible propagation rounds, sharp minimum and maximum, and the exact 2/3/4 efficient minimum seeds, exhibiting a genuine parity-controlled slowdown despite identical forcing sets. The result is structural for an infinite natural class, not an isolated computation or arbitrary parameter slice. It benchmarks efficient seed placement in a graph infection model and informs how much information static forcing polynomials omit.
